ai.title: Allow relative paths in dynamic agent templates
ai.summary: Dynamic agent templates now accept relative paths for prompt fields. `resolvePromptField` checks the template directory and project root. `validateSpawnableAgents` tolerates missing `CodebuffAI/` prefixes. Updated `dynamic-agent-service.ts` and `file-resolver.ts`.

eli5.text: If you write a prompt file inside an agent template folder, you can now point to it with a simple file name like 'prompt.md' instead of typing out a full absolute path. When templates reference other files, the system looks first in the same folder as the template, then in your main project folder, so prompts and includes keep working when you move the template between projects. Agents that don't start with the CodebuffAI/ prefix are also accepted now, and error messages tell you to check that prefix when a spawnable agent isn't recognized.

ai.title: Enforce sequential spawn for thinker agent in base prompts
ai.summary: Updated `baseAgentUserInputPrompt` in `backend/src/templates/base-prompts.ts` to explicitly forbid spawning the `thinker` agent concurrently with `file_picker` agents. The instruction now mandates waiting for file picker results before invoking the thinker. This ensures the deep thinking process operates on established codebase context.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions now tell it to wait for file-finding results before starting deeper analysis, instead of doing both at once. This affects anyone relying on the assistant's internal planning to gather accurate codebase information before reasoning about it. If you watched the assistant's process, you'd see it look up relevant files and read them completely before beginning complex problem-solving, rather than jumping into analysis while searches are still running.

eli5.text: Internal diagnostic messages about the assistant's reasoning steps now read with the status first, like "Start agent analysis" instead of "Agent analysis start", matching the same reordering applied to the closing message. ai.title: Fix dynamic agent ID collection order
ai.summary: DynamicAgentService now performs a two-pass load: collectAgentIds gathers all JSON template IDs first, then validation checks spawnable agents against the complete set. This fixes false-positive validation errors when a template references a dynamic agent defined later in the directory. Validation logic in common/src/util/agent-template-validation.ts and common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts updated to use normalizeAgentName instead of manual prefix stripping.

eli5.text: When the system loads its list of available AI assistants, it now makes two passes through the folder: first it collects every assistant's name, then it checks each assistant's instructions against that complete list. Previously, if an assistant referenced another assistant that appeared later in the folder, the system would wrongly flag it as missing because it hadn't seen the full set yet. You won't see anything differently, but you'll get fewer false error messages when setting up custom assistants that depend on each other.

ai.title: Dedup spawnable agent validation logic
ai.summary: Moved `validateSpawnableAgents` from `common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts` to `common/src/util/agent-template-validation.ts` and updated `backend/src/templates/dynamic-agent-service.ts` to use the centralized utility. The refactored function now accepts `dynamicAgentIds` directly and internally constructs the full `availableAgentTypes` list, returning a unified result object with `availableAgents` for error formatting. This eliminates duplicate validation logic and standardizes how spawnable agent errors are generated across the codebase.

eli5.text: The system's behind-the-scenes logic for checking that dynamic agents are correctly configured has been consolidated into one central place, so error messages about spawnable agents are now generated consistently across the codebase. If you're a developer maintaining or extending agent templates, you'll see that the validation function lives in a shared utility file rather than being duplicated, making it easier to fix bugs or update rules in a single spot. This is internal housekeeping with no visible impact to end users, but it makes the codebase cleaner and less error-prone for anyone working with dynamic agent validation.

ai.title: Fix dynamic agent validation in websocket-action
ai.summary: Updated `validateAgentTemplateConfigs` to accept `dynamicAgentIds`, ensuring override templates validate against dynamically loaded agents. `websocket-action.ts` now loads dynamic agents before validating overrides, passing the resulting IDs to the validator. This prevents false validation errors for spawnable agents defined dynamically.

eli5.text: When you set up an assistant to use customizable behavior templates through a live connection, the system no longer wrongly rejects templates that reference agents loaded dynamically at startup. Previously, the validation step only knew about pre-built agents, so any override template pointing to a dynamically spawned agent would be flagged as invalid. Now the system waits just long enough to discover those dynamic agents before checking your templates, so override rules that target them pass validation correctly. This is live as of today and affects anyone configuring agent behavior templates with dynamic spawning enabled.

ai.title: Infisical env overrides for worktrees
ai.summary: The `.bin/bun` wrapper now sources `.env.worktree` before invoking Infisical, allowing worktrees to override environment variables like ports. `scripts/init-worktree.ts` generates this file during setup, while `scripts/cleanup-worktree.sh` removes it upon teardown. This enables simultaneous worktree execution without port conflicts by bypassing global Infisical defaults.

eli5.text: When developers use multiple versions of the project at once (called worktrees), they can now give each one its own set of ports and settings without conflicts. During setup, a new file is automatically created in each worktree that holds its specific environment variables, and during teardown, that file is deleted. The system detects and loads these variables automatically when you start a project in a worktree, so each instance runs independently with its own configuration rather than sharing global defaults. This only affects developers working with multiple worktrees simultaneously.

ai.summary: cleanup-worktree.sh now checks git worktree list instead of directory existence before removal. Missing worktrees trigger a warning rather than a hard exit 1. Scope limited to scripts/cleanup-worktree.sh. Prevents CI or local cleanup failures when worktrees are already detached.

eli5.text: The cleanup tool that removes leftover project folders now checks the list of active worktrees first and only issues a warning instead of stopping when a worktree is already gone, so automated cleanup jobs in CI or local runs no longer fail if a worktree has already been detached.

ai.title: Add path validation for agent template configurations
ai.summary: Introduced strict path validation for `path` fields in agent template prompt overrides and dynamic fields. Rejects absolute paths and those resolving outside `AGENT_TEMPLATES_DIR` via `path.posix` normalization. Covers `systemPrompt`, `userInputPrompt`, `agentStepPrompt`, and initial/step assistant message fields. Validation failures skip further checks for the specific file.

eli5.text: Custom agent setups that pull in instructions from other files can no longer point to locations outside the approved templates folder, and absolute paths are now blocked outright; any such setup that fails this check stops right there instead of being loaded. This protects the system from configuration files that try to read from places they shouldn't, and anyone building or editing these custom agents would see these problematic paths get rejected during validation rather than silently accepted.

ai.title: Add id and toolNames validation to agent template schemas
ai.summary: Agent template schemas now enforce strict validation for `id` and `toolNames` fields. `ToolNamesOverrideSchema` in `common/src/types/agent-overrides.ts` replaces generic array handling with specific refinement logic checking against valid tool constants. `DynamicAgentTemplateSchema` in `common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts` adds similar refinement to `toolNames`, ensuring only registered tools are accepted. Invalid entries trigger errors listing available tools.

eli5.text: When setting up an assistant template, if you type a tool name that doesn't exist, the system now immediately tells you which names are allowed instead of silently accepting it. This only affects anyone configuring assistant templates that explicitly list which tools are available. If you looked right now, any invalid tool name you entered would show an error message listing the valid choices.

ai.title: Dynamic agent prompt schema now parses via json-schema-to-zod
ai.summary: Dynamic agent prompt schemas now convert via json-schema-to-zod instead of manual type switching. The promptSchema type in common/src/types/dynamic-agent-template.ts splits into optional prompt and params JSON schema objects, validated with z.record(z.any()).refine(). Backend dynamic-agent-service.ts wraps conversion in try/catch, pushing errors to validationErrors and skipping the agent. common/src/util/file.ts adds getStubProjectFileContext for test scaffolding.

eli5.text: If you build an agent that's described in a template file, the system can now read and check that template's custom input rules in a more reliable way, using a shared library instead of hand-written conversion code. When a template's rules can't be turned into something the system understands, you'll get a clear note about it and that agent will simply be skipped instead of causing a hard failure. There's also a helper added for writing tests that need a ready-made project context.

eli5.text: A new version of the assistant software shipped today that adds a few useful capabilities. The assistant can now make precise edits to specific parts of files, read documentation and source files it previously couldn't access, and automate git commits on your behalf. It also handles dynamic agent templates more reliably by accepting relative paths and validating agent configurations before use, and the worktree management scripts now support custom ports and skip missing directories gracefully. If you're using the assistant today, updating to this version enables the new file editing, documentation reading, and commit automation tools, plus the behind-the-scenes validation improvements for dynamic agent setups.

ai.title: Preserve code block indentation in docs
ai.summary: CodeDemo now preserves original indentation by passing rawContent via remark-code-to-codedemo.ts. Previous .trim() calls in code-demo.tsx stripped leading whitespace from string, array, and object children. The remark plugin extracts node.value directly into an mdxJsxAttribute, bypassing children processing when available.

eli5.text: Code samples shown in your documentation now keep their original indentation, so nested code stays aligned the way it was written. Previously, the system building those previews stripped leading whitespace from every line, collapsing indents in languages like Python where spacing matters. Behind the scenes, the documentation processor now passes the untouched code text directly to the preview component instead of cleaning it up first. You'll see properly indented code examples whenever the documentation viewer renders a code sample.

ai.title: Improve AI SDK error logging and OpenRouter cache control
ai.summary: Enhanced error logging in `ai-sdk.ts` by serializing `Error` objects via new `errorToObject` utility in `object.ts`, preserving non-enumerable properties for clearer diagnostics. Added `cacheControl` support for OpenRouter in `messages.ts` to match Anthropic's ephemeral caching behavior. These changes improve observability and provider compatibility in the core backend and shared utilities.

eli5.text: When the assistant hits a problem talking to an AI model, it now captures a fuller picture of what went wrong (including details that used to get lost in the logs), so debugging is easier. The assistant can also tell OpenRouter to cache conversation turns the same way it already does with Anthropic, which can reduce repeat work and speed things up for the same kind of request. You won't see these directly, but they help the system respond more reliably and trace issues faster.

New handler `backend/src/tools/handlers/find-files.ts` implements file retrieval via WebSocket state and search prompts. Updated `CodebuffToolHandlerFunction` params to include `agentStepId`, `clientSessionId`, and `userInputId`. Requires valid `ws`, `messages`, `fingerprintId`, and `repoId` in state.

eli5.text: The assistant can now search for and retrieve relevant files from your project when working on code tasks, instead of only reading specific files you point it to. When you ask the assistant to work on a codebase, it will automatically find files it needs to understand your project, which should make responses more accurate and complete. The developers added a switch to control how much file detail gets collected, and noted they might want to enable that on a per-project basis in the future. This feature is live and actively available when using the assistant on code-related tasks.
